summary: ObjectGenome bounds familyId/variantKey to 512 bytes but leaves component, support, mechanism, and affordance semantic keys unbounded; those keys flow into persistent ObjectState maps and the full recipe fingerprint. Add one project-owned semantic-key byte bound with deterministic 512/513-byte regressions rather than allowing arbitrarily large canonical keys.
evidence: At active generation-2 PR #318 head a136f305f432fa9c480e8d91e5d2151340795af7, isStableIdSemanticKey enforces <=512 bytes for familyId and variantKey while isSemanticKey has no byte-length bound.
component.key, supportKeys entries, mechanism.key, and affordance.key are validated only with unbounded isSemanticKey; canonical ObjectState then uses component/mechanism keys as persisted map keys.

tests/object_genome_contract_lock.luau covers 512/513-byte family/variant identity boundaries and familyVersion bounds, while tests/object_genome.luau contains no equivalent overlong component/mechanism/affordance semantic-key regression.
The finding is distinct from PR #318's familyVersion <= 2147483647 repair and does not require Studio/engine evidence.
